titre: Avengers: Doomsday Star Teases Ominous Fate for His Character
chapo: Avengers: Doomsday star Sebastian Stan has recently made comments hinting that "maybe it's time" for his character Bucky to, well, exit the MCU.
extrait: With Avengers: Doomsday a little less than a month away, Marvel shared its third and final trailer for the movie on Monday. The trailer didn't have too many surprises and mostly covered what fans had already seen in previous sneak peeks. As such, longtime Marvel viewers still have plenty of questions about the movie. Top of mind: Who's going to make it out alive? As the title implies, Doomsday will be a destructive film as universes start colliding in what are called Incursions. Fans expect at least some characters to die and not make it to Phase... whatever is next. (Who can keep track anymore?) In a recent interview, one of the film's stars has hinted that his character may not be long for the Marvel Cinematic Universe. [Ed. note: Possible spoilers for Avengers: Doomsday follow, depending on how much you want to read into an actor's comments.] Sebastian Stan has been playing Bucky Barnes/The Winter Soldier since 2011's Captain America: The First Avenger. His character has gone on quite a journey, from being a World War II sergeant to a brainwashed assassin to a Congressman. Stan says he is "always happy" to keep suiting up as the hero, as he said on the Next Best Picture podcast recently, adding, "I don't know if the decision's up to me, ultimately." While Stan said "we've done our best so far" in exploring Bucky's character, he does think there are more layers to peel back. "I don't think that that character totally got to fully live out his arc in the way that he has in the comics, for instance, or that I've wanted," Stan said. In the comics, Bucky becomes Captain America for a time after Steve Rogers' death, which is what Stan may have been referring to here. On the Happy Sad Confused podcast last month, Stan spoke about wanting to do a lost years project for Bucky and his desire to play Bucky as Captain America while he can still do action sequences. ("Sorry, Anthony," he said, referring to current Captain America actor Anthony Mackie.) "I'm always ready, but we're at that point now where I can feel it: He needs to either evolve somewhere, or maybe it's time. It's one of those," Stan said. That "maybe it's time" sure sounds like he's saying "maybe it's time" that Bucky dies. Marvel hasn't been shy about killing off characters before, as Natasha Romanoff/Black Widow and Tony Stark/Iron Man both died in Avengers: Endgame. titre: 'Maybe It's Time': Sebastian Stan Fuels Fears Over Bucky's Fate in Avengers: Doomsday
chapo: Sebastian Stan has fueled MCU fan fears that Bucky Barnes could meet his end in Avengers: Doomsday after dropping a cryptic comment that "maybe it's time."
extrait: Sebastian Stan has fueled MCU fan fears that Bucky Barnes could meet his end in Avengers: Doomsday after dropping a cryptic comment that "maybe it's time." With the massive crossover movie set to hit theaters next month, Stan was recently asked about Bucky's long-term future in the Marvel Cinematic Universe — and his response did little to calm nervous fans. Having debuted all the way back in 2011's Captain America: The First Avenger, Bucky is one of the last remaining Phase One veterans still standing on the front lines. Now, with his old pal Steve Rogers back front and center for this next installment, many fans have long suspected Bucky's 15-year arc could be about to culminate with a long-awaited reunion followed by a tragic end. "I'm always happy to keep playing him," Stan said, while appearing recently on the Next Best Picture podcast. "I don't know if the decision's up to me, ultimately. "I'm ready to take the character in all kinds of different ways," he continued, "but I can't make that decision, it's the powers that be. And I think they have a lot going on, they have a lot on their plate. Do I feel we've explored that character, there's nowhere else to go, I think we did our best? I do think we've done our best so far." To be fair to Stan, after appearances in nine films and his own Disney+ spinoff, it's hard to know exactly where the character can continue to evolve. He is arguably the most experienced member of the New Avengers team, but this is a role that could also be provided by Yelena Belova. He has long since redeemed himself for his days as the Winter Soldier. And with Steve's story (presumably) wrapped up again with these latest Avengers movies, it's unclear what else there is for Bucky to do. Stan has attempted to pitch a Bucky solo project to Marvel in the past — a thriller movie in the same vein as Denis Villeneuve-directed thriller Sicario — but noted again here that he had only received a non-commital response from MCU boss Kevin Feige. "I don't think that that character totally got to fully live out his arc in the way that he has in the comics for instance, or that I've wanted," Stan concluded. "I'm always ready, but we're at that point now where I can feel it, he needs to either evolve somewhere, or maybe it's time. It's one of those." We could be saying goodbye to Bucky Barnes in Avengers: Doomsday Avengers: Doomsday is fast approaching, and everyone seems pretty convinced Bucky Barnes isn't making it out alive. Sebastian Stan has a role in The Batman 2, which set off alarm bells for Marvel fans that the Winter Soldier might not be returning for more in the MCU – and now an update from Stan himself only seems to seal the deal. "I'm always happy to keep playing him. I don't know if the decision's up to me, ultimately," Stan said on the Next Best Picture podcast. When prompted by the interviewer that he must have some sway, Stan said: "Well, I don't know, to be honest with you. I'm ready to take the character in all kinds of different ways, but I can't make that decision, it's the powers that be. And I think they have a lot going on, they have a lot on their plate. Do I feel we've explored that character, there's nowhere else to go, I think we did our best? I do think we've done our best so far. "I don't think that that character totally got to fully live out his arc in the way that he has in the comics for instance, or that I've wanted," he continued. "I've been a big fan of the whole Black Widow of it all. But that's not the only way, you could take him in all kinds of ways. I've spoken about this Sicario-esque paranoid thriller where he just recognizes this person on the street and thinks it's a torturer from Hydra, like back in the day, and he becomes obsessed and starts following the person and realizes the person has a family. And then he's like, 'Am I crazy or is this the guy…?' and confronts the person, the guy denies it. "Kevin just sort of went, "Sounds good, uh, we'll see,'" he added with a laugh. "So, I'm always ready, but we're at that point now where I can feel it, he needs to either evolve somewhere, or maybe it's time. It's one of those." Now, while it sounds like Stan still has tons of ideas when it comes to Bucky Barnes, it also certainly sounds like he's made peace with leaving the character behind.
